extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense / Navy Contracting Officers and acquisition/procurement personnel involved in implementing OMB Circular A-76 (CITA) work
extracted.subtask_short: CITA contracting guidance for Contracting Officers
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and procedural standards describing the Contracting Officer's responsibilities across three phases (Assessment, Acquisition, Administration) for Commercial/Industrial Type Activity (CITA) A-76 service contracting, including the cost-comparison process, solicitation/award practices, and communications with stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison process (overall responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison process is the cornerstone of the contracting effort and the key element distinguishing CITA Support Service contracting from other service contracting efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a Task Group, prepare an acquisition schedule and detailed SOW, solicit contractor bids/proposals, prepare a Government in-house cost estimate (audited, sealed, submitted), determine low contract price, adjust contract price to reflect true Government cost, compare with in-house estimate to determine apparent winner, possibly conduct a pre-award survey on the lower offerer, have the Task Group complete and certify the cost comparison, subject it to audit, send recommendations to the Approving Authority for final decision, announce results to the public and allow review, then award or cancel the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a Task Group and initial responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison process commences with establishment of a Task Group to prepare an overall plan for obtaining the desired service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task Group responsibilities include establishment of an acquisition schedule and development of a detailed statement of work (SOW). The SOW will be used to solicit bids/proposals and will form the basis for the Government in-house cost estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) development
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOW must be detailed and will be used by the Contracting Officer to solicit bids or proposals and will form the basis for preparation of the Government in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOWs for services are likely longer and more complex than supply SOWs. SOWs should be prepared with measurable performance standards and surveillance plans to permit measurement of contractor progress and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government in-house cost estimate preparation and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government cost estimate is audited for accuracy and conformance to prescribed guidelines, sealed, and submitted to the Contracting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of timing issues (possible late submission) and the policy considerations about when to reveal the estimate to the public. The estimate should withstand audit and verification; discrepancies discovered by audit may present problems during award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust contract price to reflect true Government cost
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the cost comparison, it will be necessary to adjust the 'contract price' to reflect the true cost to the Government for private sector performance of the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make appropriate adjustments so the contract price represents total Government cost (including any relevant factors) before comparing to the in-house estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award survey when private-sector cost appears lower
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total private industry cost appears to be lower than the Government in-house cost estimate, the Contracting Officer may conduct a pre-award survey on the lower offerer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pre-award survey to validate the offerer's capabilities, capacity, and ability to perform under the contract terms before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group certification and audit of cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The Task Group will complete and certify the cost comparison, and it is again subjected to an audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure documentation, certification, and audit trail are complete and conform to prescribed guidelines to support the Approving Authority's decision and any subsequent public review, appeals, or protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approving Authority decision and public announcement/review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Approving Authority will make a final decision and forward it to the Contracting Officer. The Contracting Officer will announce the results of the cost study to the general public and allow time for review by interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand requirements for preliminary and final announcements, timing of public disclosure, and the public review period; plan for possible appeals and protests following announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-phase framework for CITA contracting
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework consists of three distinct phases: Phase I Assessment of the Commercial Industrial Type Activities; Phase II Acquisition (planning and contracting); and Phase III Contract Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I is ongoing but complete when a determination is made that there is no justifiable need (short of lower cost) to retain a function in-house. Phase II overlays the cost-comparison process and includes planning, solicitation/evaluation, and award cycles. Phase III begins with award and continues as long as contractor performance continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Preparation of the C/I inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the Commercial/Industrial (C/I) inventory is a Phase I activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorying functions is the basis for identifying candidate functions for review and potential contracting-out; inventory must be coordinated with higher authorities and Congressional notifications where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Establishment of review schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish review schedules for functions to be assessed for possible conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize and coordinate review schedules across field activities to permit consolidated solicitations and efficient planning; once scheduled it is difficult to change due to higher-level commitments (e.g., Congress advised of inventory schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Justification for in-house performance based on National Defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare justifications for retaining functions in-house based on National Defense considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document defense-related reasons thoroughly; ensure justifications meet directive requirements and can withstand scrutiny from auditors, GAO, and Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Justification for in-house performance based on non-availability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare justifications for in-house performance when commercial sources are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive substantiation is required showing existing firms lack capacity or technical competence; for new starts, show the probability of developing commercial capacity is low. CBD notices and other outreach must be used before relying on this exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Preparation and submission of fact sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and submit fact sheets regarding functions under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, consistent information for decision makers and interested parties; coordinate with higher authority/legal counsel when sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Grouping of similar type functions for larger solicitation packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Group similar functions to create larger solicitation packages that may attract more capable contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining functions can reduce solicitation and administration costs and attract experienced firms, but may complicate phase-in/turnover and conflict with small/disadvantaged business participation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Consideration of multifunctional solicitations (umbrella contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider multifunctional or 'umbrella' contracts (e.g., Base Operation Support Service/BOSS) for combined support functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include potential lower overall price, reduced administration, and centralized management; disadvantages include turbulent phase-in, turnover complexity, and increased coordination problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Determination of core capability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the organization's core capability requirements when assessing functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify what must be retained in-house vs what can be contracted out; use this to inform the inventory and grouping decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Preparation of local implementing directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare local implementing directives to carry out policy guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local directives should reflect the latest Circular policy and address interim guidance gaps; ensure directives are coordinated with DOD/Navy implementing guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Explore utilization of excess capacity at other Government agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore possible use of excess capacity at other Government agencies before contracting out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider interagency resources as alternatives to contracting out; document considerations and availability analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Communications with interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications with unions, private industry, Congress, and local community must be managed throughout Phase I (and the entire process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful not to imply decisions requiring higher authority; coordinate FOIA responses with legal counsel and higher authority; replies to union inquiries should be consistent, accurate, supportive of general policy, and coordinated with Naval Supply Systems Command when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBD notice requirement for establishing commercial availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a decision may be made to retain a function in-house based on inability of the private sector to satisfy the requirement, the agency must make the requirement known to a broad cross-section of American industry via Commerce Business Daily (CBD) notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a minimum, place at least three notices in the CBD over a 90-day period; for urgent requirements, two notices over a 30-day period. Also obtain assistance from GSA, SBA, and similar agencies. CBD notices alone do not require indicating A-76 or requiring contractors to demonstrate their capabilities beyond 'availability.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of informational solicitations and market surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational solicitations and market surveys may be used to determine commercial interest but have distinct disadvantages and are insufficient alone to determine no commercial source is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors may not invest time/cost in information-only submissions and responses may be inaccurate; informational or market surveys do not guarantee all potential sources were made aware. Priced informational solicitations are unacceptable as a basis for using the 'lower in-house cost' exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for sufficient contractor response (unresolved)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing directives are silent on what level of response constitutes sufficient interest to indicate private sector availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A literal reading could mean any single responsive source precludes the non-availability exception. Because this is ambiguous, rigorous documentation about capacity/competence is required when asserting non-availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for determining non-availability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: There is uncertainty about who initially determines that no commercial source is available—the Contracting Officer or the functional activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In theory source development is the Contracting Officer's realm, so the decision should rest with the CO; practically, coordination is required. Extensive documentation is necessary to justify in-house retention based on non-availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise and assist in grouping functions to enhance contractor interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer can advise functional activities on grouping similar functions or forming multifunctional solicitations to enhance contractor interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CO involvement can improve likelihood that a single firm can perform desired services; the CO role is advisory, but manpower limitations may constrain full participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of identical functions across activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize and centralize review schedules so multiple field activities review the same functions in the same fiscal year to permit consolidated solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation allows coordinated development of work statements and larger solicitations, but field coordination is often lacking; work statements frequently vary in quality between activities hindering consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service-contract-specific considerations (non-personal services and labor standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Services must be determined to be non-personal in nature to avoid creating an employer-employee relationship and service contracts usually require special clauses related to wage payments and fringe benefits under the Service Contract Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if contract terms preclude a personal relationship, actual performance may create one—monitor performance. Include appropriate Service Contract Act clauses, consider option use for extensions, and incorporate measures to monitor contractor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-solicitation and contracting phase issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Items requiring increased pre-solicitation review include methods of solicitation, sources of supply (including small and disadvantaged businesses), DAR coverage and appropriate clauses, determination of contract type, and use of options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for Procurement Administrative Lead Time (PALT), staffing, training, and contracting authority; the CO should contribute to SOW and milestone planning and maintain integrity of the overall process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation/evaluation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: During solicitation and evaluation, use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences and methods for conducting negotiations may demand closer attention; evaluation methodologies may need revision because one offerer may be the Government itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-examine philosophies of competition, consider incentive arrangements, ensure fair negotiation processes considering the Government as a potential offerer, and address pre-bid/pre-proposal conference needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award cycle differentiation and appeals/protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between solicitation evaluation factors and contract award factors; address timing issues such as late submission of the Government in-house estimate, the correct time to reveal it, and requirements for public review; understand appeals versus protest processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate discrepancies found in verification/audit; prepare for appeals or protests by ensuring documentation, transparency, and adherence to procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration considerations (Phase III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract Administration phase begins with award and continues while the contractor performs; it includes many items related to Acquisition Phase outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish surveillance plans and performance standards linked to SOWs, consider delegation of contract administration to Defense Contract Administration Services Offices, and be mindful of phase-in considerations under milestone planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and public statements constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer must ensure he makes no statements that would seem to indicate a decision has been reached on any areas requiring higher authority and must coordinate sensitive public responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate FOIA and other public inquiries with legal counsel and higher authority when required. Ensure replies to unions are consistent and coordinated with Naval Supply Systems Command where applicable; final responsibility for public inquiries rests with the field activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity of the overall process
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlying all acquisition and contracting tasks is the Contracting Officer's genuine concern to maintain the integrity of the overall process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COs must safeguard procedural fairness, documentation, auditability, and impartiality across assessment, acquisition, and administration phases to withstand GAO/audit/legislative scrutiny.
